name: Education, schooling and training
statement: "*Schooling* is an institution; *training* is the acquisition of a specific competence; *education*, on most accounts, is something broader and harder to pin down, A formation of the whole person."

internal_sources.heading_or_line: §0 Why the question has no neutral answer

notes: The sentence carries no inline source. §8.5 cites Collins, The Credential Society (1979), and Caplan for the schooling-crowds-out-education critique.

name: Peters: education as initiation into worthwhile activities
statement: "to be "educated" is not to have been trained or to have acquired information, but to have been **initiated into worthwhile activities and forms of knowledge** in a manner that one comes to value for their own sake, with breadth of understanding and "cognitive perspective"". Three criteria: it transmits something worthwhile, involves knowledge and understanding, and engages the learner's willing understanding.

cited_works.title: Ethics and Education

notes: The inline link is a StateUniversity.com page titled "John Dewey", a secondary source that does not match the Peters book. No publisher or page given.

name: Dewey: education as growth through experience
statement: Education is "**growth through experience**"; it "has no end beyond itself except *more growth*: the test of an experience is whether it leads to further fruitful experience, governed by the principles of **continuity** and **interaction**".

cited_works.title: Democracy and Education
Experience and Education

notes: Both links are secondary summaries (a blog and a notes page). No primary edition cited.

name: Whitehead: inert ideas and the rhythm of education
statement: Education must avoid "inert ideas", knowledge received but never used, combined or tested; it proceeds in a rhythm of romance, precision and generalization.

cited_works.title: The Aims of Education

notes: Title and year only; no link, edition or page.

name: Nineteen conceptions of an educated person
statement: Appendix A tabulates 19 rival conceptions of an educated person, from Greek paideia and Confucian junzi to Humboldtian Bildung, Freire's critical consciousness, Sen and Nussbaum's capabilities and the credential or signaling critique, each with its core aim and thinkers.
notes: Sources are listed in the file's Key sources section; most are encyclopedias and web summaries (Wikipedia, IEP, SEP, Britannica).

name: No neutral definition of being educated
statement: "There is no single, cross-civilizational answer to "what does it mean to be educated."" The corpus states the disagreement is a feature of the question and that any reform is a value choice that must be stated as one.
notes: Rests on the foundations/01 survey. It is an argument from comparison, and no single external work is cited for the conclusion.

name: Four convergences across traditions
statement: Across traditions thinkers agree that education is more than information, that it is moral as well as intellectual, that the teacher or community of practice matters, and that an educated person holds integrated understanding.
notes: Synthesis by the brief's author; no source at the claim.

name: Biesta: qualification, socialization, subjectification
statement: Education operates in three domains of purpose at once: qualification (knowledge, skills and dispositions to do things), socialization (induction into existing orders) and subjectification (formation of the learner as a subject). The three overlap and trade off.

cited_works.title: Good Education in an Age of Measurement
Risking Ourselves in Education: Qualification, Socialization, and Subjectification Revisited
Understanding Biesta's three purposes of education

notes: The brief separates Biesta's descriptive framework from his normative claim that measurement lets qualification crowd out the other two.

name: Labaree: democratic equality, social efficiency, social mobility
statement: Three constituencies press three goals on schools: democratic equality (the citizen, a public good), social efficiency (taxpayer and employer, a public good) and social mobility (the individual consumer, a private good). Labaree argues social mobility came to dominate and detached a credential's exchange value from learning.

cited_works.title: Public Goods, Private Goods: The American Struggle over Educational Goals

name: Eight purposes of education
statement: The brief's bottom line lists eight legitimate and partly conflicting purposes: knowledge and cultural transmission, human-capital formation, citizenship and nation-building, individual flourishing, socialization and social order, sorting and credentialing, moral formation, and emancipation.

cited_works.title: Human Capital

notes: §1.3 was read by heading and bottom line only; per-aim sources sit in Key sources (Becker, Spence signalling, Collins, Freire, Delors Report).

name: Bucket's operating definition of education
statement: "bucket.foundation reforms education. It is the operating system a person runs inside from the first year of school to the research frontier: a map of foundations, a workspace where a learner finds, quotes, checks, and organizes evidence, and a path where a student's own production enters the map as a citable contribution that outlives the term it was written in." Also: "Bucket is where a person learns to produce knowledge, starting on day one."
notes: Bucket's own position. It picks production of knowledge as the aim, which the corpus's own §5 of the Knowledge-Access Gradient says is one defensible option among contested aims.

name: Research OS five levels of interaction
statement: "Five levels of interaction with the graph, each holding the ones before it: Access ..., Awareness (where knowledge can go from here), Understanding (learning the node itself), Internalization (the learned node meets the rest of the graph), Production (a new node, built from the nodes you hold and placed among them)." The workspace "never writes the answer".
notes: The manifesto wording and the shipped tests differ. LEARNER-STATE-MODEL.md §1: Awareness is one node-open event; Understanding is one LLM-judged explanation; Internalization needs a teacher approval; Production is unconditional on submission; stage is a high-water mark with no stored decay. That file maps the ladder to ICAP, SOLO, Bloom revised and Perkins (sections 2, not read in full here).

name: The industrial model sorts
statement: "schooling is logistics for sorting a population; it is not a system for maximizing knowledge, its access, its production, its validation, or its reach for those who can go furthest."
notes: The thesis says every number is sourced in EDUCATION_PROBLEMS.md and deep/01-04; the through-line sentence itself is the author's synthesis. KAG §5 adds that sorting and credentialing have legitimate versions.

name: Bucket reforms the knowledge layer
statement: Bucket claims the layer of "how knowledge is accessed, produced, validated, and paid for" and disclaims K-12 funding, teacher pay and the low-income access crisis; "open knowledge is *necessary but not sufficient*".

statement: Six depth levels: L0 basic literacy and numeracy, L1 K-12 content, L2 undergraduate material, L3 graduate or professional depth, L4 the frontier (accessing primary research), L5 producing new knowledge.

statement: "The **canon** is the small set of buckets that have been judged to contain *foundations*, axioms, real math, rules, laws, principles, primary derivations, across seven branches". "Outcomes ... are *applications* of foundations. They live downstream of the canon".
notes: A definition by stipulation. The claim that everything downstream "could be re-derived if it was lost" (line 49) has no source.

name: Canon tier in mind
statement: "A foundational claim about cognition, language, perception, or consciousness; a method that opens the empirical study of one of those; a framework (computational, ecological, predictive) that becomes the substrate of subsequent work. Refining a single experiment is not canon-tier."

name: Promotion rule c1, c2, c3
statement: Material enters 07-mind only as c1 (primary statement by the originator), c2 (recognized edition-of-record of a c1 text) or c3 (discipline-standard reference or pedagogical-primary monograph). Surveys, textbooks and popular syntheses do not promote.

name: Outcome studies sit below the canon

name: A claim's standing depends on how it is known
statement: Founder's words in bead ros-truth epic: "A claim's standing depends on how it is known: seen and touched first-hand, reported first-hand by someone else, second-hand, recorded on video, read, derived, or proven. Tiers also depend on falsifiability, theoretical versus experimental support, whether the claim asserts existence or non-existence, and the data behind it."
notes: Quoted in the memo from BEADS-PENDING.jsonl. This is the closest thing in the repo to a stated theory of knowledge.

statement: A nominal closed set for how a claim is known: observed, reported, recorded, secondhand, read, derived, proved, asserted (default). Only proved is settled by a graph traversal; the rest need a human or pipeline assertion with a basis string.

statement: Every quantitative claim carries [bm:BucketMath.Module.name] for a Lean definition or proved theorem, [bm-open:Name] for a stated claim with no proof, or [empirical: source, date, command] for a measured number with its reproducing command.
notes: check requires every theorem outside BucketMath.Open to use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. BucketMath.Open is "empty today".

name: A resolved tag does not show the theorem supports the sentence
statement: "The lint resolves tags. It cannot tell whether the cited theorem supports the sentence, and its number heuristic misses measured claims written without digits; the critic reviews both." Concept edges, effort weights and learner evidence are inputs to cite as empirical.

internal_sources.heading_or_line: Limits; Theorems And Inputs, last row

name: Log-scale grade for numeric answers
statement: Two positive values are within tolerance p/q when max^q <= 10^p * min^q; Correct is tolerance one half and Close is 3/20. The grade is symmetric, scale invariant, monotone in the ratio, and no pair of positive rationals sits on the boundary at one half.
formal: BucketMath.Grade.within_symm, within_scale, within_of_closer, no_exact_boundary, correct_accepted_with_epsilon, close_correct (lean/BucketMath/Grade.lean)
notes: The proofs cover the arithmetic of the grade. No source is given for choosing half an order of magnitude as correct; vectors in lean/vectors/fermi-grade.txt suggest Fermi-estimate items.

name: Review scheduling clamps stay in bounds
statement: For any raw values, the clamped difficulty, stability and interval sit inside their bounds (interval between 1 and 3650 days), and stored values give positive arguments to every power and logarithm in a review.
notes: MATH-CONTRACT: "this covers the clamps alone, and the end-to-end review is checked by replay". No theorem states that FSRS predicts recall.

name: Guess-corrected score
statement: For c correct of n four-choice items, s = (c/n - 1/4)/(3/4), so chance scores 0 and a perfect run scores 1. H_p is s over solo items, J_p over pair items, A is the model's s over the same pair items.
notes: Lean carries the score as integer numerator 4c - n over 3n and proves the bounds and the zero at chance. Validity of four-choice recognition as a measure of judgment is unproved; the paper lists it as a limitation.

name: Multiplier
statement: "The multiplier is m_p = J_p / max(H_p, A), reported as null when max(H_p, A) < 0.1": the joint score over the better single agent.
notes: A definition with no measured value. Not in Lean. The paper makes D the primary statistic and reports m_p beside it. At a ceiling m_p collapses toward 1.

name: Gain
statement: "the gain is D = J_p - max(H_p, A)"; "D is the primary statistic".
notes: No measured value. The decision rule reads only the sign of D, so 0.02 and 0.30 fall in the same cell.

name: Retention
statement: "Retention is R_p = H_p(t + 7 d) - H_p(t) over the solo items": the change in the unaided score on the same items after seven days.

cited_works.authors: Roediger, Henry L. and Karpicke, Jeffrey D.
cited_works.title: Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention

formal: retestDue_gt (papers/human-ai-multiplier/lean/Bucket/Multiplier.lean) proves only that the retest time is later than the probe time
notes: Seven days is fixed and unjustified by a source; the paper says thirty or ninety days is a different quantity. Regression to the mean inflates R_p; a no-AI control arm is planned.

name: Learning
statement: "Learning is L = J_p(t + 7 d) - H_p(t + 7 d): at the retest, the score on items first seen with the model minus the score on items first seen alone, both unaided".
notes: This is Bucket's only stated measure of learning impact from AI. It is a between-half difference on the same items, so it measures retained recognition, and it does not measure transfer to new items.

name: Dependence
statement: "Dependence is flagged when the 95% interval of J_p - H_p lies above zero and the 95% interval of L includes or lies below zero". "The gain was there with the model in the room and gone a week later."
notes: Lean proves two logical consequences of the definition on integer interval bounds. Whether the flag detects real dependence in people is untested.

name: The hai probe
statement: A probe is 40 unseen four-choice items in 20 pairs matched on tier and on whether the model was right; one item of each pair is answered solo and one with the model's answer and a rationale of at most 25 words shown after 20 seconds; no feedback until an unaided retest of all 40 items seven days later.

cited_works.title: Bootstrap Methods: Another Look at the Jackknife

notes: Intervals are 95% percentile bootstraps over pairs, 2,000 draws. A is one run of claude-opus-5-5 at low effort. Tested on fixed data only.

name: Instrument status: no person measured
statement: The bank is frozen at 998 items with 68 flagged and none cleared. "No AI scores have been collected, no probe has been run". "There are no values of H_p, A, J_p, m_p, R_p or L to report."
notes: Dated 2026-10-07. Item mix: 482 recall, 240 apply, 177 derive, 90 teach, 9 conceptual; learning-to-learn has 29 items.

name: Items needed for a usable interval
statement: A half-width of 0.10 on J_p - H_p near a true score of 0.5 needs about 342 items per condition; 0.15 needs about 152. The design target is a half-width of 0.10 after 17 probes and no trend before 5 retested probes.
effect: 342 items per condition for half-width 0.10; one person; planning figure
notes: Tagged [empirical: stats.ts halfWidthItems, evaluated by hand]. Seventeen weekly probes is about four months per person before one interval is tight.

name: Decision rule: augment, withhold or replace
statement: Per task class and per person: D > 0 and L >= 0, augment with the person's attempt first; D > 0 and L < 0, augment as a means only and practise unaided in Learn; D <= 0, leave with the person; A > H_p with J_p near A, candidate to replace outside Learn with the person reviewing.
notes: The paper: "a rule with no result behind it yet". Thresholds on effect size wait for data.

name: Three rules joining learning system and probe
statement: Planned: draw probe items from atoms at the learner's frontier; report R_p beside the FSRS predicted recall R(7, S); update mastery from the solo half only in a dependence cell, so "a model's answer could never raise a concept into accepted mastery on its own".

name: Divergence hypothesis
statement: A group answering with the same model converges on its answers and phrasings, so the range of ideas narrows even where each score rises. Planned test: open items, mean pairwise cosine distance among a group's answers, solo against pair.

cited_works.authors: Doshi, Anil R. and Hauser, Oliver P.
cited_works.title: Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces the collective diversity of novel content

notes: The cited study is given as the basis for the prediction; the paper does not state its design, so the grade here is the label for Doshi and Hauser as described ("a study"). The open-item bank is unbuilt.

name: Knowledge state, closed state and frontier
statement: The catalog is a DAG of concepts with a mandatory-prerequisite relation; a knowledge state is a set K of concepts, closed when every immediate prerequisite of a member is a member; a concept outside K is ready, on the frontier, when all its prerequisites lie in K.
formal: Closed, Required, Path, After (papers/human-ai-multiplier/lean/Bucket/Learning.lean; same in lean/BucketMath/Learning.lean)
notes: This is the paper's formal definition of what a learner knows: set membership. It has no degrees, forgetting or transfer.

name: Necessary additions
statement: From a closed mastery state, every feasible learning sequence that reaches target t contains every concept in R(t, M) = C(t) minus M, so its length is at least |R(t, M)|.
notes: Holds under assumptions A1 to A5. A4 assumes nothing is forgotten during the episode.

name: Attained minimum learning path
statement: Listing each element of R(t, M) once in a prerequisite-first order is feasible, reaches t, and attains the minimum length |R(t, M)|; with fixed costs the same order attains the minimum effort.
notes: Lean takes the enumeration and order as inputs; it does not verify a topological sort or the TypeScript planner. Effort means a fixed cost per concept, an input no data supplies.

name: More mastery never lengthens the path
statement: If M1 is a subset of M2 then R(t, M2) is a subset of R(t, M1) and the remaining distance does not grow.
notes: This is the formal content behind the impact line "learning systems that build on what a person already knows".

name: Diamond: chain planning undercounts
statement: With F to A, F to B, A to T, B to T and empty mastery, the chain F, A, T never reaches T; any feasible sequence needs four steps.

internal_sources.heading_or_line: §The minimum prerequisite learning problem, Figure prereq

name: Assumptions A1 to A5
statement: The theorems hold when every encoded edge is mandatory and none is missing (A1), the closure is finite (A2), restricted mastery is closed (A3), a step adds one concept and nothing is forgotten in the episode (A4), and costs are fixed (A5). "A1 ... is a property of the curriculum that no proof can supply."

internal_sources.heading_or_line: §The minimum prerequisite learning problem; §Limitations, The three connecting rules

notes: No source or study supports any real prerequisite edge in the Academy graph. MATH-CONTRACT lists concept edges as inputs to cite as empirical.

name: Knowledge region: coverage G and extent r
statement: With confirmed flags m(v) on a catalog factored over axes, g_j is the confirmed share on axis j, G the catalog share confirmed, and r the weighted root mean square of g_j; G <= r <= sqrt(G), and none decreases when flags only rise.
formal: coverage_monotone, squared_extent_monotone (papers/human-ai-multiplier/lean/Bucket/Learning.lean; lean/BucketMath/Learning.lean) cover natural-number cases only
notes: The real-valued propositions are human proofs outside Lean. The paper: "neither carries a meaning of intelligence or general competence"; a new catalog or basis ends the comparison.

name: Planner matches brute force on small graphs
statement: Across 1,099 DAGs of one to five nodes and 57,060 cases, the candidate planner's distance error, omitted-required count and readiness-error count against an independent breadth-first search were all zero.
effect: 0 errors in 57,060 enumerated cases; synthetic graphs, no people
notes: Software verification. "Neither involves a person." Untested above five nodes except by fixtures.

name: Synthetic learner prediction experiment
statement: On 1,200 synthetic learners, Brier scores were 0.24633 (intercept), 0.23475 (item effects) and 0.18649 (axis and prerequisite covariates) on 4,800 test responses.

internal_sources.heading_or_line: §Learning system results, Statistical experiment, Table ls

effect: Brier reduction 0.04826 over the item baseline; 600 synthetic test learners
notes: "The generator that produced the learners also contains the axis and prerequisite predictors, so their Brier advantage is expected by construction". No real learner or item bank.

name: FSRS-5 retrievability as shipped
statement: Predicted recall t days after a review at stability S is R(t, S) = (1 + F t/S)^(-1/2) with F = 0.9^(-2) - 1 = 19/81, so R(S, S) = 0.9; stability and difficulty update with 19 default weights.
notes: The paper cites the code and no FSRS publication, dataset or fit. Default weights, unfitted to Bucket learners. "The retention axis is a prediction from the FSRS state, and the protocol's R_p will be the observation that tests it."

name: Mastery as shipped
statement: "mastery is their product": M = P^alpha R^beta with P = sigma(theta - b_apply), b_apply = -0.2, R = R(90, S), alpha = beta = 1, clipped to [0, 1]; "a concept counts as mastered at M >= 0.7".
notes: No source for the product form, the 0.7 threshold, the 90-day horizon or b_apply. The paper: the exponents are "a hook for a later fit rather than a fitted parameter" and the mapping from M >= 0.7 to accepted mastery "is a product decision that no theorem covers". "Nothing in Lean touches the mastery formula, FSRS, assessment validity or any learner outcome".

name: Four artefacts that mimic an effect
statement: Ceilings, task drift between probes, regression to the mean and the practice effect of the retest can each mimic or hide a gain; the design answers with matched pairs, a within-item retest, a planned no-AI control arm and reading L as a between-half difference.
